newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street stocks drift lower.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street stocks drift lower.

text.p: Wall Street stocks drifted lower Monday as investors braced for the corporate earnings season, which starts this week.
Just after 1 p.m. EST, the Dow Jones industrial average was off 6.15 points at 6,697.64, coming off the record close of 6,703.79 set Friday when the blue-chip index jumped 78 points.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 13-10 on active volume of 257 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq Composite was off 0.03 of a point at 1,331.99 The American Stock Exchange index was up 1.73 at 587.77.
Analysts said investors were holding back after Friday's powerhouse reversal and rally as they awaited the slew of fourth quarter earnings.
Among blue-chip issues, J.P. Morgan & Co. Inc. gained 2-1/2 to 102-1/4 after reporting better-than-expected results.

"You are starting the earnings season and everyone is bracing for the fourth quarter reports. J.P. Morgan was an auspicious start to the season and that is helping the market as much as anything today," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany Corp.
He said the stock market was in a defensive mode with strength focused in sectors such as regional and money centre banks, food, soft drinks and tobacco.
"The worst performing groups are the oils and chemicals, groups that are sensitive to the economy," he said. "We've had a couple of weeks during which the economic news was upbeat.
"Today, things are starting to creep back in the other direction. It is clear that this market is not convinced that the economy will remain strong."
Joseph Barthel, chief investment strategist at Fahnestock & Co., said that a correction was likely to be forthcoming.

"Anytime you have an overbought market with rising interest rates you normally get a correction," he said. "I think that by month's end we will be in a position to start a correction, probably more concentrated in large cap stocks rather than in the small caps."
Among special situations, American Standard Cos. jumped 3-1/4 to 43-1/2 after the company disclosed that it rejected a merger proposal from Tyco International Ltd. Tyco was down 3/8 at 54-1/4.
DeKalb Genetics Corp. was up 2 at 60-3/4 on tronger than expected quarterly earnings.
C-Phone Corp. gained 1-13/16 to 18-1/16. The company said last Friday that it will develop a family of video conferencing products with Analogue Devices Inc.
